introduction.definition: An emergency ventilation fan is an explosion-protected axial fan that starts automatically when gas detectors alarm, purging the building to dilute a leak below its flammable range. The impeller and casing are a non-sparking pair, the motor is flameproof, and a gravity damper closes when the fan stops.
applications: Compressor houses, analyser shelters, battery rooms
Pump houses and enclosed process modules

pressure.title: Start on gas, purge fast, never ignite
pressure.description: Emergency ventilation runs at high rate when gas detection reaches its first alarm (often ≈ 10–20 % LEL), diluting a leak below its flammable range and venting it outside. Equipment in the air stream must suit the hazardous-area zone (Ex d / Ex e motor, temperature class) and the impeller–casing pair must be non-sparking (e.g. aluminium/bronze vs steel) — a rub must not cause a spark. The gravity damper closes when the fan stops, keeping weather out. Supplies are typically on essential power.

video_tutorials.title: Emergency Ventilation Fan — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Emergency Ventilation Fan.
An emergency ventilation fan is an explosion-protected axial fan that starts automatically when gas detectors alarm, purging the building to dilute a leak below its flammable range.
The impeller and casing are a non-sparking pair, the motor is flameproof, and a gravity damper closes when the fan stops.
Typical applications include compressor houses, analyser shelters, battery rooms; pump houses and enclosed process modules.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Fan Casing (spark-resistant: non-sparking rotor/casing material pair), Aluminium / Bronze Axial Impeller (adjustable pitch).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Emergency Ventilation Fan.
Check standby status and alarms.
Run test; bump-test detector.
Inspect tip clearance, Ex integrity.
Watch for fan fails to start: no ventilation on alarm. Common cause: power / starter fault.
Watch for impeller rub: noise, spark risk. Common cause: bearing wear.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
